query: Knucklebones {At the fireside table the regulars are throwing knucklebones for coppers. There's a space on the bench, and a copper on the table with your name on it, if you want it.|Knucklebones again. The old carter who always wins is winning. He pats the bench beside him.|The regulars wave you over before you've shut the door. The landlady says the game's been dull without you, and charges you for it.} Play it straight {The bones fall your way three throws running. The carter says it's beginner's luck, then that it's been going on too long for that.|You win the pot, a handful of coppers and a lot of goodwill. The landlady takes a cut for the fire.|You play badly and win anyway. The table says that's the worst kind of player.} {The bones roll every way but yours. The carter buys you a cider out of your own losses, with great ceremony.|You lose, cheerfully and steadily. The regulars like you better for it.|Down a few coppers by the end. The carter says you've got the hands for it, just not the luck.} Buy the round and just watch {You buy the round and watch. By the end you know everyone's name and the carter's whole family tree.|A round for the table, and a seat by the fire with no stakes at all. It's the best evening you've had all month.|You buy the round. The landlady writes it on your tab, to the penny, and the table drinks your health.} See how the bones will fall {You glimpse each throw before it leaves the hand and bet on what you've seen. You win, and win, and the carter starts to look at you with great interest.|A moment ahead every time. You win the pot and buy the next round with it, which helps your conscience a little.|You see the bones fall before they're thrown. You take the pot, and leave before the carter works out how, which he is getting close to.}
